configuration.title: Modkit MK3
configuration.disabledContributions.desc: Contribution ids to switch off, one level below `modkit.extensions`: an extension may ship several codecs and you may want only some of them. A disabled contribution stays in the inventory and loses activation, so a file only it could read opens as raw bytes with the diagnostic `x3.host/contribution-disabled` — and the switch is still there to turn it back on. Takes effect when the window reloads.
configuration.disabledExtensions.descrip: Extension coordinates to switch off without removing their cards or contributions from the inventory. Individual contribution choices are preserved and become effective again when the extension is enabled. Takes effect when the window reloads.
configuration.extensionRegistry.descript: Catalog file or HTTPS URL used by the extension manager. Opening the Extensions view reads only its local cache; the registry is contacted only by `Modkit: Refresh Extension Catalog`. `MODKIT_EXTENSION_REGISTRY` is used when this setting is empty. Remote catalogs also require an Ed25519 key map in `MODKIT_EXTENSION_TRUSTED_PUBLIC_KEYS`; remote artifact origins stay blocked unless listed in `MODKIT_EXTENSION_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`.
configuration.contentSourceConfig.descri: Absolute path to a trusted desktop content-source provider JSON. Leave empty to use Modkit's automatic local sources (selected game installation, Battle.net cache, player documents and editor wizards). An online account/publishing provider may be supplied here and takes effect without restarting the window.
configuration.extensions.description: Extension directories to load beside the ones that ship with this build. Each item is either a path, or an object with `path`, an optional `id` the directory is expected to declare, and an optional `enabled` flag. Directories named here are loaded as installed artifacts and never run in the extension host process.
command.setCodecDefaultEditor: Modkit: Open Files of a Codec With Modkit by Default
command.syncEditorAssociations: Modkit: Sync Editor Associations With Codec Settings
configuration.nonDefaultContributions.de: Contribution ids that stay enabled but do NOT become the default editor for their formats. An enabled codec is the default viewer for the formats it claims; listing it here keeps the codec working while the built-in editor stays the default. Modkit only ever removes associations it added itself, so an "Open With → Set Default" chosen in VS Code is never overwritten.
configuration.defaultEditorForTextFormat: Also make Modkit the default editor for text-first formats (txt, xml, json, md, csv, ini, yaml, galaxy, sc2layout and the rest of that list). Off by default: those open in an editor people type into, and taking that over on install would replace editing with viewing. Modkit is always reachable for them through "Reopen Editor With".
The `workbench.editorAssociations` patterns Modkit wrote. Modkit removes only these, never an association you set yourself. Edited automatically; listed here so what the extension changed is visible.
